text:
marta: quick heads-up — ran a small probe on continuous-batcher tweaks, saw weird p99 blips when kernel flip happens during KV prefetch. attaching notes below.

sanjay: can you paste the probe config? was this with the new decode-rate buckets?

marta: yes — used three decode-rate buckets (slow: <15 t/s, mid: 15-35 t/s, fast: >35 t/s) + prompt-length quartiles. admission token_budget set to {slow:80, mid:48, fast:24} and max_batch  = {slow:32, mid:24, fast:12}.

lucas: hmm those budgets are fairly aggressive for fast streams. where do we flip kernels?

marta: kernel flip threshold is 128 cached tokens / request; runtime switches to tiled-attn kernel on long KV warmups. The blip happens when a few fast decode requests land and hit flip while a larger slow request in the same batch forces KV prefetch eviction.

ada: @marta can you share sample perf numbers? even rough p50/p95/p99 and token/s throughput?

marta: sure — small table from the probe (1000 requests):
```
bucket             | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tok/s avg | batches/sec
slow-length-high   | 42      | 120     | 320     | 10.2      | 18
mid-length-med     | 28      | 80      | 210     | 22.3      | 34
fast-length-low    | 18      | 60      | 400     | 48.7      | 72
```
Notes: fast-length-low p99 spikes to 400ms when mixed with slow-length-high in same admit window.

perf-bot: automated-profile: build/2026.03.12-rtprobe — observed 6.4% p99 increase vs baseline on node-type g4dn.xlarge during canary window. Kernel-selection trace shows flip events cluster at 120-140ms into decode.

lucas: that aligns with KV eviction timeline — when a large prompt triggers prefetch, the smaller fast requests lose KV slot and suffer a synchronous disk read fallback.

ada: can we mitigate by tightening the admission policy so batches prefer homogeneity? e.g., sliding window that prefers same decode-rate bucket rather than FIFO?

marta: idea: change queue-slicer to weigh coalescing score = alpha * decode_rate_bucket_score + beta * length_bucket_score + gamma * waiting_time. set alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1 for probe. That should reduce mixed batches by ~40% in sim.

sanjay: another approach: lower token_budget for slow-length-high slightly (80->64) to reduce KV prefetch footprint, and bump fast max_batch to 16 to keep throughput. tradeoff: slow p95 might go up ~8%.

lucas: agree on trying both: prefer homogeneity + small token_budget trim. We should run an A/B on 5% traffic for 24h. Add logging to capture kernel_flip and kv_eviction events per-batch.

marta: prepared canary config:
```
canary:
  traffic: 5%
  queue_slicer:
    weights: [0.6,0.3,0.1]
  buckets:
    decode_rate_bins: [15,35]
    length_quartiles: auto
  token_budget_overrides:
    slow: 64
    mid: 48
    fast: 24
  max_batch_overrides:
    slow: 28
    mid: 24
    fast: 16
  log_events: [kernel_flip, kv_eviction, batch_cohort_id]
```

ada: please also add a metric for "mixed_batch_rate" (percent of batches with >=2 decode_rate buckets) and report p99 delta per bucket.

perf-bot: scheduled job: nightly-compare for canary vs baseline, will report p50/p95/p99 and mixed_batch_rate every hour.

sanjay: one more ask — include kernel-selection histogram (time-of-flip relative to request start) in the reporting. that helped earlier root-cause.

marta: done. I'll kick off the canary at 10:00 PT and watch the first 2 hours.

lucas: if p99 for fast bucket still spikes, we should consider prefetch reservation: reserve N KV slots per fast cohort to avoid eviction. cost impact estimate?

marta: rough calc: reserve 4 slots per fast-worker -> ~6% memory overhead, should cut eviction-induced tail by ~70% in sim. put behind feature flag.

ada: sounds good. sync in 2h if anything noisy. thanks! :thumbsup:

perf-bot: canary started at 1943211800 (10:00 PT). monitoring now.

marta: (follow-up) after 90m, mixed_batch_rate dropped from 0.28 -> 0.11, fast p99 down from 400ms -> 210ms, slow p95 increased +6%. saving looks worth it for latency-sensitive product flows.

sanjay: nice. let's bake changes into default policy but keep token_budget trim as an opt-down for throughput-oriented fleets.

lucas: file an RFC for kernel-reservation feature + cost model. I'll draft initial doc.

marta: created RFC draft: /docs/rfcs/2026-03-batcher-reservation.md (WIP)."
